slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Palisade raise prices in 2027 while churn is rising and, if so, where and by how much, to grow ARR at least 15% with net revenue retention above 100%?
Is rising churn a sign that customers reject our price?
Will mid-market and enterprise customers accept a rise at renewal?
Can SMB take a rise now that Inkwell sells at $9?
What does each option add to ARR, and does it reach 15%?
How should we roll out the rise in 2027?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO, deciding the 2027 pricing plan with the leadership team
ARR up at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M; Net revenue retention above 100% overall; Price changes only at renewal, and within enterprise contract terms
Leadership meeting on the 2027 pricing plan, December 2026
New plans or packaging to answer Inkwell; Renegotiating enterprise price caps; The 2027 new-customer sales plan

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay for the product, and test SMB before touching it
Rising churn comes from the 2025 promotion, not from core customers leaving over price
–	Other SMB churn is 2.1% a month, from 2.0% a year earlier
–	Better onboarding of the cohort cuts SMB churn by a tenth, not half
Mid-market and enterprise are the safer place for a 10% rise at renewal
–	A 10% higher price did not slow 2024 mid-market sign-ups
–	Enterprise adds only about $0.8M, as 40% of its ARR renews in 2027
An SMB rise is a bet on Inkwell: it breaks even at twice the 2023 reaction
–	Our win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38%
–	An 8% rise on non-promotion SMB nets about $0.7M
The targeted rise adds about $4.3M and keeps the 15% target in reach
–	The 12% plan yields about $7.6M, not $10.3M
–	New customers need to add only about $0.6M of ARR
Reprice where customers stay in January, and test SMB in Q1
–	The promotion cohort keeps today's price and gets an activation push

A cross-check, not a second estimate
▪	The exit survey reports 34% for all SMB churners in H1 2026; the implied share is within a few percentage points
▪	The gap can come from different response rates in the two groups, which the brief does not give
▪	A cohort churning far less than about 4.9% a month could not produce the jump from 19% to 34%

The 12% plan beats the targeted rise only while SMB reactions stay mild
▪	SMB's reaction scales with the size of the rise: 12% against 8% in 2023
▪	At 2.6 times the 2023 reaction, the 12% plan falls below the targeted $4.3M
▪	The promotion cohort is repriced too, though it already churns at about 4.9% a month
▪	Lost SMB deals to Inkwell from a higher list price are not counted
